outcome: Still open in general: no source found since 26 January 2024 settles the conjecture, and the 2025 and 2026 papers themselves describe it as open. Two in-window results bear on it. Gille, Izquierdo and Lucchini Arteche (arXiv, 2 Jan 2025) prove H¹ triviality for complete discretely valued fields of dimension 2, a restricted class. Nguyen (arXiv, 9 Mar 2026) proves an equivalence with a pseudo-reductive generalisation and rational-point results for pseudo-semisimple groups over global function fields and non-archimedean local fields, which adds no new field or semisimple group to the statement. No AI system is credited with any step on this problem.
problem_asks: The statement, unpacked. (A) Groups: every simply connected semisimple algebraic group G, of any type (A, B, C, D including trialitarian D4, E6, E7, E8, F4, G2), including products of such factors. (B) Fields: every perfect field F of cohomological dimension at most 2, in any characteristic (this includes p-adic fields, global fields, function fields of surfaces, pseudo algebraically closed fields and others). (C) Conclusion: H¹(F, G) is trivial for every pair in (A) and (B), i.e. every G-torsor over F has an F-rational point. Not asked by this bullet, recorded so the later pass can see the boundary: the converse (which Merkurjev and Suslin proved over perfect fields), Serre's 1994 imperfect-field version using separable cohomological dimension, and Serre's Conjecture I (cohomological dimension 1, connected groups), which is a separate bullet.

events.what_happened: Diego Izquierdo and Giancarlo Lucchini Arteche, 'Transfer principles for Galois cohomology and Serre's conjecture II', arXiv:2308.00903. Proves transfer principles for the cohomological dimension of fields and applies them to Serre II. Headline: Serre II for characteristic 0 fields implies Serre II for positive characteristic fields. Theorem E (Section 4.3, per the v3 HTML): if Serre II holds for countable fields of characteristic 0, it holds for arbitrary fields. The paper states that this recovers, unconditionally and over imperfect fields, the conjecture for groups with no factors of type E6, E7, E8 or trialitarian D4 (Corollary 4.17). Journal: Advances in Mathematics vol. 480, article 110532, dated 1 Nov 2025, per search excerpts only; the ScienceDirect page could not be opened.
events.revisions: v1 2 Aug 2023; v2 14 Dec 2023; v3 9 Sep 2025 ('final accepted version'). Published in Advances in Mathematics, 2025 (per search excerpts).
events.delivers: A reduction, not a new case. Serre II for all perfect fields of cohomological dimension at most 2 and all simply connected semisimple groups is reduced to countable fields of characteristic 0 (Theorem E) and to characteristic 0 in general (headline). The unconditional consequences the paper states are for imperfect fields and for groups without E6, E7, E8 or trialitarian D4 factors. Those are outside this bullet's perfect-field hypothesis, and they reuse Bayer-Fluckiger and Parimala's perfect-field result. No new perfect field or group in the bullet is settled.
events.remains: The conjecture itself. The introduction says: 'Contrary to Serre's conjecture I, this one remains open, although a lot has been done in particular cases.' Remaining: the countable characteristic 0 case that Theorem E assumes, and every perfect cohomological-dimension-2 case not covered elsewhere.

events.what_happened: Philippe Gille, Diego Izquierdo and Giancarlo Lucchini Arteche, 'Central simple algebras, Milnor K-theory and homogeneous spaces over complete discretely valued fields of dimension 2', arXiv:2501.01403 (math.RA; cross-listed AG and KT). v1 abstract, with K a complete discretely valued field with residue field of dimension 1, not necessarily perfect, which is equivalent to K having dimension 2: period equals index for central simple K-algebras; for each prime p, Milnor K-theory mod p classes are symbols; and 'Serre's Conjecture II holds for the field K', i.e. H¹(K, G) is trivial for every semisimple simply connected K-group G. v2 (19 Feb 2025) restates the setting as complete discretely valued field of dimension 2 and gives Theorem 1.3: H¹(K, G) = 1. The introduction says the result was already known when the residue field is perfect (Kneser's p-adic work; Bayer-Fluckiger and Parimala [BP95]; Berhuy, Frings and Tignol [BFT07] for types), and the paper removes that assumption.
events.revisions: v1 2 Jan 2025 (setting: complete DVF with residue field of dimension 1, not necessarily perfect; abstract already states Serre II for K). v2 19 Feb 2025 (setting restated as complete DVF of dimension 2; same Serre II statement; Theorem 1.3). v2 introduction cites '[ILA24]' for a reduction of Serre II to countable characteristic 0 fields of dimension 2; I could not identify that citation with a specific document.
events.delivers: Serre II for one class of fields: complete discretely valued fields K of dimension 2 (Theorem 1.3), for every semisimple simply connected K-group G. The new content is removing the perfect-residue-field assumption that earlier results carried, per the paper. Perfect such K are the only ones the bullet's hypothesis reaches. The paper states its result for K without a perfectness hypothesis, which is a stronger statement than the bullet on that class. Restricted class: this settles no other perfect field of cohomological dimension at most 2.
events.remains: Every other perfect field of cohomological dimension at most 2, for every simply connected semisimple group. The paper's own text: 'This conjecture remains open, although a lot has been done in particular cases.' The Section 6 remarks also expect that characteristic zero can be removed from the hypotheses of Theorem 6.7, which is a different theorem about the boundary map of H¹ into H²(K, μ).
events.time_since_posted: about 21 months from v1 to 13 Oct 2026. No independent public engagement found: no journal publication, comment, review or citing paper surfaced in searches. The authors presented the work: Lucchini Arteche's BIRS talk 'Period-index and Serre's Conjecture II for complete discretely valued fields of dimension 2' (30 Sep 2025; title only, no abstract). Gille's LMS talk of 12 Mar 2026 was described in a search excerpt as covering the discrete valued case based on this work; its PDF could not be read. These are the authors' own talks, not checks.
events.doubts: No specific doubt found in the text read. Points to weigh: all three authors are specialists in the area and co-authored with one another; the perfect-residue-field case was already known, so the new content is one assumption removed; no independent reading or journal status found. The v2 HTML was read in two passes covering Sections 1 to 6; the excerpt returned did not include an acknowledgements section.
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for this class of fields: H¹ is trivial for every semisimple simply connected group over such K. Does not contradict anything in the statement.

events.what_happened: Mac Nam Trung Nguyen (written Nguyen Mac Nam Trung in the paper header; Institute of Mathematics, Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology, Hanoi, per a search excerpt), 'Serre conjecture II for pseudo-reductive groups', arXiv:2603.08061 (math.NT, cross-listed math.AG; 7 pages). Abstract: the conjecture is stated as a prediction about torsors under semisimple simply connected groups over fields of cohomological dimension at most 2 and imperfection degree at most 1; the author generalises it to pseudo-reductive groups and proves the two versions equivalent; unconditionally, every torsor under a simply connected pseudo-semisimple group over a global function field or a non-archimedean local field has a rational point.
events.revisions: v1 only, 9 Mar 2026, as of retrieval.
events.delivers: (a) An equivalence: Serre II for semisimple simply connected groups is equivalent to a version for pseudo-reductive groups. (b) Rational points for simply connected pseudo-semisimple groups over global function fields and non-archimedean local fields. For this bullet, semisimple groups over those two field classes were already settled (Harder for global function fields; Bruhat and Tits for local fields, both as cited in the paper's background). So (b) adds groups outside the bullet and no new field class or semisimple group within it. (a) is a reformulation and proves no instance of the bullet by itself. Only the abstract was read; the PDF text could not be extracted.
events.remains: The bullet as stated: every perfect field of cohomological dimension at most 2 and every simply connected semisimple group. The abstract calls the conjecture a prediction and does not claim it is proved. Also open after this paper: E6, E7, E8 and trialitarian D4 over general perfect cohomological-dimension-2 fields, and the general case.
events.time_since_posted: about 7 months from v1 to 13 Oct 2026. No comment, response or citing paper surfaced in the searches run; arXiv shows v1 only.
events.doubts: Not yet checked by anyone I could find. Only the abstract was read, so the equivalence proof and the pseudo-semisimple argument are unchecked. Single author. The arXiv comment field says only '7 pages'.
events.direction: Partly confirms: rational points for pseudo-semisimple groups over two field classes, and an equivalence with a generalised conjecture. It does not claim the bullet's conjecture is proved and calls it a prediction.

events.what_happened: Alexandre Lourdeaux and Anis Zidani, 'Conjecture I for unirational algebraic groups over imperfect fields', arXiv:2604.05148. Proves Serre's Conjecture I (connected linear groups, cohomological dimension at most 1) for unirational algebraic groups over imperfect fields, using pseudo-reductive groups and the structure of wound unipotent groups, and extends related Galois cohomology results. Discounted: this is Serre's Conjecture I, not Serre II.
events.delivers: A Serre I analogue for unirational groups over imperfect fields of Kato dimension at most 1. It concerns connected linear groups in cohomological dimension 1, not semisimple simply connected groups in cohomological dimension 2. It does not bear on the bullet's H¹ vanishing.
events.remains: All of Serre II, which this paper does not address.
events.time_since_posted: about 6 months. Not assessed, since the paper is outside the bullet's scope.
events.direction: Confirms a Serre I analogue for unirational groups over imperfect fields. Does not bear on which way Serre II goes.

events.what_happened: Haocheng Ju and 15 coauthors, 'Automated Conjecture Resolution with Formal Verification', arXiv:2604.03789 (cs.LG, cs.AI). Framework with an informal reasoning agent, Rethlas, and a Lean 4 formalisation agent, Archon. The abstract says: 'Using this framework, we resolve an open problem in commutative algebra and formally verify the resulting proof in Lean 4 with essentially no human involvement.' Discounted for this bullet: the resolved problem is in commutative algebra. From a search excerpt of the appendix (the PDF text could not be read), the paper also reports a test on rational conjugacy classes of 1-parameter subgroups of algebraic groups, with a lemma that H¹(k, U) is trivial for split smooth connected unipotent U, and a sourcing gap for a wound-unipotent reduction. A search excerpt says the appendix output came from GPT-5.5 xhigh and another says GPT-5.5 Pro gave an incorrect proof in a comparison; these two excerpts conflict and neither was verified.
events.delivers: Nothing on this bullet. Per the abstract, a commutative-algebra problem is resolved. The appendix's Galois-cohomology lemma concerns split unipotent groups, not simply connected semisimple groups, and does not reach Serre II.
events.time_since_posted: about 6 months. Not assessed, since the result is outside the bullet's scope.
events.machine_checked: Lean 4 formalisation of the commutative-algebra proof, per the abstract. Sorry status and URL not verified. Not relevant to Serre II.
events.doubts: From the appendix excerpt only: the system could not access a key reference for one ingredient and cited a survey whose stated theorem was partial, so a reduction needed correcting. This concerns the appendix's different problem.
events.direction: Nothing on Serre II. On the commutative-algebra problem, it claims a resolution.

events.what_happened: Jason Michael Starr, 'Rationally simply connected varieties and pseudo algebraically closed fields', arXiv:1704.02932, submitted 10 Apr 2017 (v1 only; no journal given on the arXiv page). Proves Serre II for perfect fields of cohomological dimension 2 that are pseudo algebraically closed, provided the field has characteristic 0 or contains primitive roots of unity of orders prime to the characteristic. Uses rational simple connectedness. Also shows the fields are C₂ fields and proves period equals index for their Brauer groups.
events.delivers: Serre II for a restricted class: perfect pseudo algebraically closed fields of cohomological dimension 2 in characteristic 0, or containing the required roots of unity. Not all perfect cohomological-dimension-2 fields.
events.remains: Perfect cohomological-dimension-2 fields that are not pseudo algebraically closed, and PAC fields in positive characteristic without the required roots of unity.
events.time_since_posted: about 9.5 years to 13 Oct 2026. Later engagement not established from the searches.
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for this class of fields.

events.what_happened: A. J. de Jong, Xuhua He and Jason Michael Starr, 'Families of rationally simply connected varieties over surfaces and torsors for semisimple groups', arXiv:0809.5224 (v1 30 Sep 2008; only version listed). Abstract: under suitable hypotheses, a form of a projective homogeneous variety G/P over the function field of a surface over an algebraically closed field has a rational point; as a consequence, 'we complete the proof of Serre's Conjecture II in Galois cohomology for function fields over an algebraically closed field.' Published in Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS, 2011 (per a search excerpt; the Numdam page was not opened). A search excerpt of a Starr seminar abstract describes the result as the split case; the arXiv abstract does not restrict to split groups.

events.remains: Function fields of surfaces over non-algebraically-closed fields, and other perfect fields of cohomological dimension 2.

events.what_happened: Merkurjev and Suslin: Serre II for groups of inner type 1A_n (special linear type and related inner forms), via their work on K-cohomology of Severi-Brauer varieties and the norm residue homomorphism. A search excerpt dates the relevant paper to 1983, and Starr's lecture notes (search excerpt) call it the first major case. The year is from secondary sources and was not verified.

events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for type 1A_n groups.

events.what_happened: Bayer-Fluckiger and Parimala: Serre II for classical groups (types A, B, C, D, excluding trialitarian D4), F4 and G2 over perfect fields of cohomological dimension at most 2. Cited as [BP95] by Gille, Izquierdo and Lucchini Arteche (2025), Section 6: 'According to [BP95] and [BFT07], Theorem 6.1 holds for semisimple simply connected groups of types A, B, C, D (except trialitarian D4), F4 and G2.' The year is taken from the citation label; the original was not read.

events.what_happened: Chernousov, Mathematische Annalen, 2003 (per a search excerpt): for quasi-split simply connected groups of types 3,6D4, E6 and E7 over perfect fields of characteristic not 2 or 3, the kernel of the Rost invariant is trivial, which gives Serre II for these groups when cohomological dimension is at most 2. A search excerpt of Gille's E7 notes says the stronger result holds for all, not necessarily quasi-split, exceptional groups of types 3,6D4, E6 and E7 over (C2)-fields. A search excerpt says Chernousov's E8 results are partial. Not read in full.
events.delivers: Serre II for quasi-split simply connected groups of types 3,6D4, E6 and E7 over perfect fields of cohomological dimension at most 2 (characteristic not 2 or 3), as reported by secondary sources. Partial for E8.
events.remains: Non-quasi-split forms over general perfect fields of cohomological dimension at most 2, and E8.
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for the quasi-split cases listed.

events.what_happened: Berhuy, Frings and Tignol, 'Serre's Conjecture II for classical groups over imperfect fields' (Bielefeld preprint 228 per search result; year from the citation label [BFT07] in Gille, Izquierdo and Lucchini Arteche 2025). Proves a strong imperfect-field version for classical groups: if the separable dimension of F is at most 2 for every torsion prime of G, every G-torsor is trivial, as summarised in a search excerpt. Discounted for this bullet, which concerns perfect fields only; this is a different-hypothesis version.

events.remains: Nothing of the bullet is affected. The perfect-field case of the same groups is covered by the Bayer-Fluckiger and Parimala event above.

The year and exact statement of Kneser's result were not established; the original was not located.

disputes.summary: Wikipedia's Serre's conjecture II article says the conjecture 'has been proven for all groups over all perfect fields', and that it 'remains open for anisotropic E6, E7, E8 groups and trialitarian D4 group over imperfect fields'. The 2023 Izquierdo and Lucchini Arteche paper says 'this one remains open'. The 2025 Gille, Izquierdo and Lucchini Arteche paper says the conjecture 'remains open'. The 2026 Nguyen preprint calls it a prediction. No source for the Wikipedia perfect-field sentence was found. Older expert material conflicts with it: a 2016 Gille slide deck (search excerpt) says other exceptional groups are 'widely open', and a Yong Hu slide deck (search excerpt) says it is open for a few exceptional groups, e.g. E8. Gille's 2009 survey page gives no status statement; only its abstract was read.

summary: Serre's conjecture II, as stated in the bullet, is still open. The strongest sources all say so: the 2023 Izquierdo and Lucchini Arteche paper, the 2025 Gille, Izquierdo and Lucchini Arteche paper, and the 2026 Nguyen preprint. Within the window (from 26 January 2024) there are two items that bear on it, and neither settles any new instance of the bullet's full statement. (1) Gille, Izquierdo and Lucchini Arteche, arXiv:2501.01403 (v1 2 Jan 2025), proves H¹(K,G)=1 for every simply connected semisimple group over a complete discretely valued field of dimension 2; this is a restricted class, and the paper says the perfect-residue case was known (Kneser, Bayer-Fluckiger and Parimala) and it removes that hypothesis. The reading that it is 'a case' fits the bullet's wording; the reading that it settles 'the conjecture' does not, since the paper calls the conjecture open. (2) Nguyen, arXiv:2603.08061 (9 Mar 2026), proves an equivalence with a pseudo-reductive version and rational points for pseudo-semisimple groups over global function fields and non-archimedean local fields. Only the abstract was read. For the bullet, the semisimple case over those fields was already known (Harder, Bruhat-Tits), so this adds no new field or semisimple group. The Izquierdo and Lucchini Arteche 2023 paper (arXiv 2 Aug 2023, so pre-window; journal publication Advances in Mathematics 480, 2025, per search excerpts) reduces the conjecture to countable characteristic 0 fields and to characteristic 0 in general; it adds no new perfect case. Its reduction appears to be the '[ILA24]' cited by the 2025 paper, but I could not confirm that identification, so later_work_cites_it is left null. Older partial results from 1975 to 2017 (Harder, Bruhat-Tits, Merkurjev-Suslin, Bayer-Fluckiger and Parimala, Chernousov, Berhuy-Frings-Tignol, de Jong-He-Starr, Starr 2017) are recorded as events; most come from secondary citations, and the Kneser entry has no date. The Wikipedia article's sentence that the conjecture is 'proven for all groups over all perfect fields' conflicts with every 2023 to 2026 source read, and no source for it was found, so I treat it as unsupported and record it as a dispute. AI involvement: I found no AI system credited with any step on Serre II. The nearest hit is arXiv:2604.03789 (Rethlas and Archon, April 2026), which the abstract says resolves a commutative-algebra problem; a search excerpt of its appendix describes a Galois-cohomology lemma on split unipotent groups for a different question, so I recorded it as a discounted event with its AI credits and did not put it under this bullet. OpenAI's August 2026 ten-problem Astra release was checked in its repository (openai/ten-proofs, opened): none of the ten results is Serre II or Galois cohomology. Epoch AI's FrontierMath open-problems page (opened) lists 49 problems and displays 10 'solved by AI' items; none of those 10 is Serre-related, and I did not see the other 39. The Kato-Kuzumaki papers by Gambardella and by Gambardella and Shaw are not about Serre II. No Lean or Coq formalisation of Serre II was found in searches. Review: no comment, response or independent check of the 2025 or 2026 papers surfaced; the 2025 paper's journal status is unknown. Close calls: whether the 2025 result counts as 'a case' of the bullet (it does on its own words, as one class of fields); whether Nguyen's equivalence counts as progress (it is a reformulation, not a proof of any instance); and whether Wikipedia's perfect-field claim is an error or cites a source I could not find.
competing_reading: The strongest case for a different reading is Wikipedia's. If 'proven for all groups over all perfect fields' is correct, then the bullet's full statement is settled before the window, every in-window item restates known results, and the bullet should be counted as solved earlier. Against it: the three most recent sources (2023, 2025 and 2026) each say the conjecture is open; the Wikipedia sentence has no source I could find and is internally odd, since it also says the conjecture is open for imperfect fields and for some groups. A second reading treats the 2025 Gille, Izquierdo and Lucchini Arteche paper as settling a case of the bullet, which is what the wording invites: 'Serre's Conjecture II holds for the field K'. Against a broad reading of 'the bullet': K is a complete discretely valued field of dimension 2, a small subclass of perfect fields of cohomological dimension at most 2. A third reading would count Nguyen 2026 as progress because it proves rational points for a new group class; against that, the new groups are not in the bullet, and the equivalence is a reformulation.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The source behind Wikipedia's 'proven for all groups over all perfect fields' sentence, or confirmation that it is an error. (2) The journal status of arXiv:2501.01403, and the Advances in Mathematics record for arXiv:2308.00903 (the ScienceDirect page returned 403 and the publication details are from search excerpts). (3) Whether the '[ILA24]' cited in the 2025 paper is arXiv:2308.00903 or a different 2024 document. (4) The full text of arXiv:2603.08061 to check the equivalence proof and whether it yields any instance of the bullet over a field class not already covered. (5) Gille's 2026 LMS survey talk slides (the PDF was unreadable in my tools) and his E7 notes, to confirm the status claims for E6, E7, E8 and trialitarian D4 over perfect fields. (6) The full text of arXiv:2604.03789, including its appendix and acknowledgements, to pin down which model was used there and confirm there is no Serre II content. (7) Any later comment or citation of arXiv:2501.01403 or arXiv:2603.08061, which would show whether specialists have engaged with them.

event.what_happened: Philippe Gille, Diego Izquierdo and Giancarlo Lucchini Arteche, 'Central simple algebras, Milnor K-theory and homogeneous spaces over complete discretely valued fields of dimension 2', arXiv:2501.01403 (math.RA; cross-listed AG and KT). v1 abstract, with K a complete discretely valued field with residue field of dimension 1, not necessarily perfect, which is equivalent to K having dimension 2: period equals index for central simple K-algebras; for each prime p, Milnor K-theory mod p classes are symbols; and 'Serre's Conjecture II holds for the field K', i.e. H¹(K, G) is trivial for every semisimple simply connected K-group G. v2 (19 Feb 2025) restates the setting as complete discretely valued field of dimension 2 and gives Theorem 1.3: H¹(K, G) = 1. The introduction says the result was already known when the residue field is perfect (Kneser's p-adic work; Bayer-Fluckiger and Parimala [BP95]; Berhuy, Frings and Tignol [BFT07] for types), and the paper removes that assumption.
event.revisions: v1 2 Jan 2025 (setting: complete DVF with residue field of dimension 1, not necessarily perfect; abstract already states Serre II for K). v2 19 Feb 2025 (setting restated as complete DVF of dimension 2; same Serre II statement; Theorem 1.3). v2 introduction cites '[ILA24]' for a reduction of Serre II to countable characteristic 0 fields of dimension 2; I could not identify that citation with a specific document.
event.delivers: Serre II for one class of fields: complete discretely valued fields K of dimension 2 (Theorem 1.3), for every semisimple simply connected K-group G. The new content is removing the perfect-residue-field assumption that earlier results carried, per the paper. Perfect such K are the only ones the bullet's hypothesis reaches. The paper states its result for K without a perfectness hypothesis, which is a stronger statement than the bullet on that class. Restricted class: this settles no other perfect field of cohomological dimension at most 2.
event.remains: Every other perfect field of cohomological dimension at most 2, for every simply connected semisimple group. The paper's own text: 'This conjecture remains open, although a lot has been done in particular cases.' The Section 6 remarks also expect that characteristic zero can be removed from the hypotheses of Theorem 6.7, which is a different theorem about the boundary map of H¹ into H²(K, μ).
event.time_since_posted: about 21 months from v1 to 13 Oct 2026. No independent public engagement found: no journal publication, comment, review or citing paper surfaced in searches. The authors presented the work: Lucchini Arteche's BIRS talk 'Period-index and Serre's Conjecture II for complete discretely valued fields of dimension 2' (30 Sep 2025; title only, no abstract). Gille's LMS talk of 12 Mar 2026 was described in a search excerpt as covering the discrete valued case based on this work; its PDF could not be read. These are the authors' own talks, not checks.
event.doubts: No specific doubt found in the text read. Points to weigh: all three authors are specialists in the area and co-authored with one another; the perfect-residue-field case was already known, so the new content is one assumption removed; no independent reading or journal status found. The v2 HTML was read in two passes covering Sections 1 to 6; the excerpt returned did not include an acknowledgements section.
event.direction: Confirms the conjecture for this class of fields: H¹ is trivial for every semisimple simply connected group over such K. Does not contradict anything in the statement.

judgement.why: The only post-snapshot event that touches the statement is Gille–Izquierdo–Lucchini Arteche (Jan 2025): H¹(K,G)=1 for complete discretely valued fields of dimension 2. That is one class of fields, so it is a case. It is unreviewed and credible: the authors are established specialists, and no doubt specific to the paper is recorded. The class is not empty of new perfect instances: a perfect characteristic-0 K can have an imperfect residue field, and the paper removes exactly that perfect-residue assumption. Nguyen 2026 proves things about pseudo-semisimple groups, which the statement does not ask about, and an equivalence with a generalised conjecture. On semisimple groups it adds nothing new, so it is a variant. Lourdeaux–Zidani is about Conjecture I, so it is a variant. Ju et al. resolve a commutative-algebra problem and have nothing on Serre II, so its scope is none. Its AI role (generated) is recorded from its own quote but does not bear on this problem. Izquierdo–Lucchini Arteche 2023 is before the snapshot (v3 is the accepted version, with no new mathematics shown). It is a reduction, so its scope is none; the journal acceptance makes it digested. The classical results before the snapshot are each cases. None of them is whole. Kneser has no date, but every source treats it as long-known prior work, so I placed it before the snapshot.
judgement.doubts: Wikipedia's claim that the conjecture is 'proven for all groups over all perfect fields' has no source and is contradicted by the 2023–2026 specialist papers, so I did not credit it. Verification of the pre-snapshot classical journal results rests on secondary citations; none was opened. Kneser's date is unknown. Nguyen was read only at abstract level.
